question_text:
A clinical study is studying new genetic gene-based therapies for children and adults with sickle cell disease. The patients were informed that they were divided into two age groups since younger patients suffer from different complications of the disease. The pediatric group is more likely to suffer from which of the complications?
I. Splenic sequestration
II. Avascular necrosis
III. Pulmonary hypertension
IV. Acute chest syndrome
V. Nephropathy?

                    ### Question
                    A clinical study is studying new genetic gene-based therapies for children and adults with sickle cell disease. The patients were informed that they were divided into two age groups since younger patients suffer from different complications of the disease. The pediatric group is more likely to suffer from which of the complications?
I. Splenic sequestration
II. Avascular necrosis

IV. Acute chest syndrome
V. Nephropathy?

opb. I, IV, V
opc. I, II, IV
opd. III, IV

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In pediatric patients with sickle cell disease, the most common complications include splenic sequestration and acute chest syndrome. Splenic sequestration occurs more frequently in younger children due to splenic dysfunction, which is a well-documented risk in this age group. Acute chest syndrome is also prevalent among pediatric patients, often triggered by infections and vaso-occlusive crises. In contrast, avascular necrosis is more commonly seen in older patients due to chronic pain and joint issues, while pulmonary hypertension and nephropathy are less common in younger patients. Therefore, the pediatric group is more likely to suffer from complications I (Splenic sequestration) and IV (Acute chest syndrome). This aligns with the consensus in the medical literature regarding the complications of sickle cell disease in different age groups.
